_folder_in_drive (file_question.py:221-245) follows Terms: a relative path gives its dirname; an absolute path is resolved against the normpath'd mount via commonpath, with relpath and dirname; an empty directory gives TOP_OF_DRIVE.
_type_label (file_question.py:248-257) matches the three .loft labels in Terms, and the Type is computed inside load_material, as item 1.2 requires.

Template: S179 is the first line after Rules:; S181a/b/c come immediately before the Answer line on every branch; S180 replaces the passages-only sentence only when image and not frames, on the passages branch; the passages-only opener carries the new wording.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: _type_label reads the .loft file (through _loft_source) for every .loft whatever its file_type, while the indexed_files read session is still open and before load_material may return None for a file with no rows.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Any question on a .loft triggers one extra bounded read of up to 64 KB; the user sees no difference except a negligible delay.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A stored file_path that is empty or None gives no Folder line; Terms defines Folder only for relative and absolute paths.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Only hand-edited or malformed index rows have no file_path; the prompt then just lacks the Folder line.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A drive whose mount is '/' places every absolute path inside it, so the Folder line carries the full host directory without its leading slash.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: It needs a mount configured at the filesystem root, which an ordinary setup does not use.

regression_risks: Material gains three required fields with no default; any future or out-of-tree construction of Material without them will raise TypeError. In this tree it is constructed only in load_material (file_question.py:439, 593, 596).
The I7 baseline goldens (file_question_today_*.json) were created in this same change; if any was recorded from code other than d9b7daf, I7 would compare against the wrong baseline and still pass.
test_coverage: Every path in RUN is covered for: the block at the start of the user prompt (I1), the S179/S181 positions (I4/I6), the new opener (I4), and a byte-for-byte comparison with today's requests after the additions are taken out (I7).
Folder rows cover relative and absolute paths, a mount with and without a trailing slash, a sibling prefix, outside the mount, no mount, and NFD names (I2), plus mount absence on every path (I3).
.loft Type labels are covered for youtube, vimeo, generic, a missing url or provider, an unreadable body and a missing file, including no log output.
S180 placement is checked on passages-and-image and on the first request of the text-only retry; its absence is checked on six other branches.
The history ordering test covers only the passages-only path.
